cohort: 243 women seeking postpartum care at the Academy of Family Medicine, Al-Madinah Almunawarah, between June 2021 and December 2021
finding: The prevalence of postpartum depression was relatively high (31.68% major depression, 20.57% mild depression), and was significantly associated with the number of prior children, child health, income status, and family support.
mod_finding: The study found that most babies (72.4%) were born via normal vaginal delivery (NVD) while only 27.76% were born via caesarean section, but did not report if mode of delivery was significantly associated with postpartum depression.
